settings.label: Access token
settings.meaning: Calls Intercom's REST API as the app: contacts, companies, events, conversations and notes.
settings.whereToFind: Developer Hub › your app › Configure › Authentication: Access token. Intercom has no test mode: use a separate development workspace, with its own app, for test.

settings.label: Workspace ID
settings.meaning: The workspace the Messenger opens: its app_id. Intercom calls it both the workspace ID and the app ID.
settings.whereToFind: The part of the Intercom address after /apps/ (app.intercom.com/a/apps/<workspace ID>/…), or app_id in Settings › Channels › Messenger › Install.

settings.label: Data region
settings.meaning: Where the workspace's data is hosted: us (the default), eu or au. It picks the REST API's address and the Messenger's api_base.
settings.whereToFind: The workspace's Intercom address: app.intercom.com is us, app.eu.intercom.com is eu, app.au.intercom.com is au.

settings.label: Messenger API secret
settings.meaning: Signs the JWT that tells the Messenger who the signed-in user is (Messenger security), so nobody can open another user's conversations.
settings.whereToFind: Settings › Workspace › Security › Messenger: the JWT setup's secret key. Test and production workspaces have different keys.

settings.label: Client secret
settings.meaning: Checks that a webhook came from Intercom: each notification is signed with the app's client secret.
settings.whereToFind: Developer Hub › your app › Configure › Basic information: Client secret.

operations.name: contacts.create
operations.purpose: Creates a user (or a lead), with the app's own id as external_id.

operations.name: contacts.update
operations.purpose: Updates a contact's email, name, custom attributes and the rest.

operations.name: contacts.get
operations.purpose: Reads one contact by Intercom's id.

operations.name: contacts.findByExternalId
operations.purpose: Reads one user by the app's own id (users only, not leads).

operations.name: contacts.search
operations.purpose: Finds contacts by their attributes (email, external_id, role…), a page at a time. New contacts can take a few minutes to appear.

operations.name: contacts.attachCompany
operations.purpose: Attaches a company to a contact.

operations.name: companies.createOrUpdate
operations.purpose: Creates the company with this company_id (the app's own id), or updates it when it exists.

operations.name: events.create
operations.purpose: Records that a user did something (a data event). Intercom ignores a repeat with the same user, name and created_at.

operations.name: conversations.list
operations.purpose: Lists conversations, a page at a time.

operations.name: conversations.search
operations.purpose: Finds conversations by their attributes (contact_ids, state, updated_at…), a page at a time.

operations.name: conversations.get
operations.purpose: Reads one conversation, with its parts.

operations.name: conversations.reply
operations.purpose: Replies to a conversation as an admin: a comment the user sees, or a note only teammates see.

operations.name: conversations.close
operations.purpose: Closes a conversation as an admin, optionally with a last message.

operations.name: notes.create
operations.purpose: Adds a note to a contact, which only teammates see.

signature.description: The header is sha1= followed by the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA1 of the raw request body, keyed with the app's client secret. A retried notification keeps its id (notif_…) but its body changes (delivery_attempts), so dedupe on the body's id.

events.meaning: Intercom checking the endpoint: sent on demand and from time to time, always subscribed.
A user or lead started a conversation.
A visitor, lead or user replied in a conversation.
A teammate replied in a conversation.
A teammate added a note to a conversation.
A conversation was assigned to a teammate.
Two contacts were merged: data.item is the one that remains, with merged_from naming the other.
